cards.statement: Someone can be close to a relative even if they live in another city.
cards.explanation: Close describes the relationship, not necessarily physical distance.

cards.statement: Get on with someone means have a good relationship with them.
cards.explanation: Get on with describes a friendly or successful relationship.

cards.statement: A close-knit family has strong links between its members.
cards.explanation: Close-knit describes a group with close, strong relationships.

cards.statement: A close-knit family may still live in several different cities.
cards.explanation: Close-knit describes emotional closeness, not a shared address.

cards.statement: An only child has no brothers or sisters.
cards.explanation: Only child describes a child without siblings.

cards.statement: A person can rely on someone and still disagree with them sometimes.
cards.explanation: Relying on someone means trusting their support; it does not mean agreeing about everything.

cards.statement: Your aunt's child is normally your sibling.
cards.explanation: Your aunt's child is your cousin, not your sibling.

cards.statement: Make up means invent a new family member in this lesson.
cards.explanation: In this relationship context, make up means reconcile after an argument.

cards.statement: Look up to someone means admire them.
cards.explanation: Look up to expresses admiration or respect.

cards.statement: A blended family can include children from earlier relationships.
cards.explanation: Blended families combine members from previous relationships.

cards.statement: The expression get on with is followed by the person involved.
cards.explanation: We say get on with someone.

cards.statement: Make up after an argument means become friendly again.
In-laws are relatives connected through a partner or marriage.
cards.explanation: In-laws are relatives of your partner or relatives by marriage.

cards.statement: Fall out with someone describes a disagreement.
cards.explanation: Fall out with someone means have a serious disagreement.

cards.statement: Relative and relationship can always replace each other in a sentence.
cards.explanation: A relative is a family member; a relationship is the connection between people.

cards.statement: Rely on someone means distrust them completely.
cards.explanation: Rely on means trust someone to help or do something.

cards.statement: Keep in touch means stop communicating with someone.
cards.explanation: Keep in touch means continue communicating.

cards.statement: Look up to your aunt is the natural way to say you take care of her.
cards.explanation: Look up to means admire; look after means take care of.
